newsitem.title: UK: BT says it should not be subject to UK windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: BT says it should not be subject to UK windfall tax.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Sunday repeated its view that its inclusion in a planned government windfall tax on privatised utilities would not be justified.

A BT spokeswoman told Reuters "We do not believe that the windfall tax should apply to BT. We are not a monopoly. We have 250 licensed competitors, we have paid corporation tax and continued to invest in Britain."
But she declined to say whether BT would mount a legal challenge if it was included in the one-off levy, which Britain's new Labour government intends to unveil in its first budget.

The Observer Sunday newspaper earlier said BT definitely would be among the companies subjected to the levy. It cited the new Paymaster General Geoffrey Robinson, whom it decribed as an "architect" of the tax, as saying "It's hard to see how (BT) could be left out. It's only a question of how much it will have to pay." The Labour Party, which swept to power on May 1, has kept its list of target companies secret, although water and electricity groups are known to top its list. There has been considerable uncertainty over whether BT would be included, especially as the company went out of its way to cultivate the Labour Party when it was in opposition. Finance Minister Gordon Brown wants to use funds from a windfall tax for a programme to get the long-term jobless and young people into work. In an interview with The Observer, Brown said he expected to raise more than the three billion pounds ($4.9 billion) needed for the welfare-to-work programme.
